description: Dependency updates (ADR-048 'Supply chain and repository settings', WP-6 D9): grouped, weekly, three days after release, never merged without a review.

packageRules.description: Updates that change what an image runs are titled fix(deps) (ADR-049, WP-7 Q2): runtime packages in the catalog and the base image in the Dockerfiles. The pull request must also run `pnpm release-inputs`, so its squash commit touches the release-inputs.txt (or Dockerfile) of exactly the services whose image changes and release-please releases a patch of each. Not a postUpgradeTasks entry: the hosted Renovate runs no repository commands, so the command is run by hand on the branch.
Development-only packages never reach an image, so they keep the chore(deps) title in every update type, majors included. The same names as the dev tools group below; keep the two lists in step.
Development tools, non-major updates in one pull request. Matched by name: the catalog in pnpm-workspace.yaml has no dependency type.
The Nest family, non-major updates in one pull request.
OpenTelemetry, non-major updates in one pull request.
GitHub Actions, SHA and version comment together, in one pull request. Majors stay alone. A digest update with no version change means a moved tag: review it as a warning sign.

Node in one pull request: the version in .nvmrc (nvm manager) and the base image the Dockerfiles pin in `ARG NODE_IMAGE` (dockerfile manager, tag and digest) move together, as scripts/docker-base-image.test.mjs requires. Titled fix(deps): the new base releases every service whose Dockerfile it touches.

customManagers.description: Container images run with `docker run` in the workflows, the root scripts and the infra scripts (gitleaks and zizmor from GHCR, Trivy, restic, the docker CLI and the restore Postgres from Docker Hub), written as name:tag@digest. One pull request updates every file that names the image. GHCR returns no release dates, so the cooldown holds those updates on the dependency dashboard until a box there is ticked; Docker Hub images carry dates and follow the cooldown.
